messages:
acme_ops (customer): Hey, we're seeing streaming responses get truncated ~30s in and our client reconnects. Happens only from our EU region and after a spike in requests. Partial events, then a disconnect. Request id: rdx-cc-0192.
kevin (support): Sorry about that — can you paste the client logs + the eventstream headers? Any 401s or 5xx in the tail?
acme_ops (customer): attaching quick tail: 
```
2026-03-15T14:12:03Z INFO chunk 0 sent 4820 bytes
2026-03-15T14:12:08Z WARN client read stalled 25s
2026-03-15T14:12:33Z ERROR write failed errno=11 EAGAIN after 65536 bytes - aborting stream
2026-03-15T14:12:33Z INFO connection closed by server (code=0)
```
No 401s in that snippet.
kevin (support): hmm EAGAIN after exactly 64KB boundary looks like an intermediary (proxy) buffering then not draining. Two quick checks: 1) can you repro with curl locally? 2) confirm if you're behind a corporate proxy/load balancer. Also, did you see a sudden billing increase? reconnects can replay payloads.
maya (oncall): tagging eng-runtime. From runtime side, we generally handle short writes by retrying; abort path is triggered if write fails with EAGAIN and send buffer appears stuck for >10s. This log looks like the runtime triggered graceful abort because client read stalled.
raj (eng-runtime): quick note: recent change to socket flush code tightened the abort window to 12s during heavy batching to avoid stuck GPUs. That might surface as truncated SSE if the client is slow to read.
acme_ops (customer): We're not behind a special proxy, but our edge team confirmed a managed WAF that might coalesce responses. Repro steps I used: 
```
curl -v -N \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=redwood-small" | pv -qL 10
```
If I throttle reader (pv -L) I can reproduce reliably in ~20-40s.
kevin (support): good repro, thanks. Two immediate mitigations: reduce server batch size (batch_tokens=64) or enable runtime option `sse_force_chunked_flush=true` in Dedicated/Private. For hosted, I can open a config to reduce default continuous batching for your org. Want me to flip it?
acme_ops (customer): please try reduced batching on our org. Also noticed a billing spike during reconnect storms, we want to avoid that.
maya (oncall): I'll run a focused trace for rdx-cc-0192 and look for socket-level errors and proxy RTTs. raj, any chance we can soften the abort behavior to treat EAGAIN as transient for a bit longer? Maybe exponential backoff for short writes instead of immediate abort?
raj (eng-runtime): We can, but it's a tradeoff — keeps GPUs tied up if client is actually gone. Proposal: for SSE paths, extend the EAGAIN window to 30s and add a hard cap on per-request GPU token lifetime. Also add better logging: include `sndbuf` size and `tcp_info` RTT in the log line.
logs-bot: trace rdx-cc-0192 attached: /s3/traces/rdx-cc-0192/2205126789/trace.json.gz
kevin (support): actionable plan: (1) I lowered batching to 64 for acme_ops in prod EU (temporary) — please validate. (2) maya will collect pcap + tcp_info. (3) raj to prototype a softer EAGAIN path on a canary. (4) customer to test with curl throttling and confirm no more truncation.
acme_ops (customer): after the change I'm seeing full streams for 45+ minutes while throttling. No more truncated chunks. Thanks. One more oddity: in one trace we saw a mid-stream 401 right before reconnect — token refresh race?
kevin (support): if token refresh fails mid-stream you can get 401s and client will reconnect then re-auth which looks like a replay. For long lived streams use session tokens with refresh BEFORE starting the stream or include `Authorization: Bearer <long-lived-session>` handshake. We'll also check server logs for token TTL refresh errors.
maya (oncall): got a pcap — confirms proxy coalescing and delayed ACKs around those times, and tcp_send buffer was 64KB. I'll escalate to infra to patch proxy config to disable response coalescing for SSE endpoints.
raj (eng-runtime): I'll open a canary PR for 30s EAGAIN window + extra logging. If safe, we can roll in 48hrs.
kevin (support): marking resolved for now since customer reports fixed with temporary batching change. Tracking follow-ups: proxy config change (infra), runtime canary roll (eng-runtime), guidance doc on avoiding token-midstream-401 (docs). :thumbsup:
acme_ops (customer): confirmed no billing spike after we applied client-side backoff + your batching change. Cheers! :party:
